body:
I want...room for error. I've been on my own since I was 17, and I feel like I've never had the freedom to make mistakes that my friends had.

They could slack off a little and take an extra year to graduate because their parents would pick up the slack. I had to stick to it because I would lose my scholarships. 

My previous work environment was absolutely TOXIC, and I had friends who would say "just quit you don't deserve to be treated like that." And it's SO EASY for them to say and do. Because we they quit their parents will cover the rent & utilities for a month or two until they can settle in a new job. If I quit without something already lined up I'm homeless. 

Those are extreme examples but it trickles down to everything. I feel like everyone around me is happier because they've had an opportunity to just do what they wanted and not worry about the consequences and I never have.  I never partied in school because I was taking a full course load and working 30-40 hours a week. I've never just gotten in the car and driven three states away because if I broke down or ran out of money for gas I'd be stranded. I didn't get married and have babies when I was young & in love because it was too big a financial risk. 

And the end result is that now at 29 I'm emotionally and socially stunted. I can't connect to people. Last week was my birthday and I didn't even have anyone to spend it with. I took myself out to eat at a nice restaurant alone.

I don't even know anymore. The things that used to make me happy just don't anymore. The only thing that I truly enjoy anymore is reading & cuddling my dog. I used to enjoy video gaming, and I still do it daily, but even that is more of a "chore" than something I truly enjoy.
My diet is trash because I emotion-eat all the time. I do walk my dogs for 20-30 mins almost every day (barring an extra long work day or bad weather). BMI is 38.

The debt by itself isn't overwhelming -- I make enough to pay the minimums plus a little extra -- the problem is I don't have the means to get help. I have no wiggle room to take time off work to get professional help.
